errors.text_span: The “Δ Accuracy” series is an orange dashed line with diamond markers and orange error bars; it is about 0.36 at 0.71, drops to around 0.10 at 0.73 and about 0.08 at 0.79, rises to roughly 0.24–0.28 at 0.82–0.83, is about 0.11–0.16 at 0.85–0.86, peaks near 0.46 at 0.87, falls to about 0.04 at 0.90, rises again to around 0.41 at 0.91 and about 0.44 at 0.93, and finishes near 0.08 at 1.00. The “Initial Accuracy” series is a green dash-dot line with square markers and green error bars; it begins around 0.55 at 0.71 and about 0.63 at 0.73, increases to roughly 0.92 at 0.79, declines to about 0.70 at 0.82 and about 0.64 at 0.83, rises to around 0.78 at 0.85, drops to about 0.45 at 0.87, increases to about 0.83 at 0.90, fluctuates between roughly 0.46 and 0.83 across 0.91–0.99 (e.g., about 0.46 at 0.93 and about 0.83 at 0.95), and ends near 0.90 at 1.00.
errors.evidence: The description provides a point-by-point recitation of nearly every data value for the "Δ Accuracy" and "Initial Accuracy" series. This level of detail is excessive and makes it difficult for a reader to grasp the overall trends and key features of the data, such as the major peaks and troughs.
The description does not mention the legend that is present at the top of the chart, which is a key element for understanding which line corresponds to which data series.
